courses.title: Analytical Chemistry I
courses.description: Discussion of chemical equilibrium, separations, and bioanalytical methods.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Analytical techniques for chemistry and biology
courses.description: An introduction to analytical techniques used to answer biological questions with a focus on the roles of small molecules from the human and environmental microbiome.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Metabolomics
courses.description: Experimental and data science workflows in modern metabolomics studies.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Mass Spectrometry
courses.description: Topics include sample handling, ionization methods, MS/MS, and quantitative analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Sensors
courses.description: Origins of selectivity, principles of transduction mechanisms, construction and applications of modern chemical sensors.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Electroanalytical Chemistry
courses.description: Coulometry, electrolytic separations, polargraphy chronopotentimetry, coulometric titrations, voltammetry, and hydrodynamic electrochemical methods of analysis.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Analytical Separations
courses.description: In-depth understanding of separation processes and the mechanisms underlying the design and development of modern separation techniques.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
courses.description: Reaction mechanisms in organic chemistry, including the concepts of physical organic chemistry, reactive intermediates, and complex functional group transformations.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Identification of Organic Compounds
courses.description: Description of molecular structure and identification of organic compounds using spectroscopic techniques.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
courses.description: Physical methods in organic chemistry; determination of reaction pathways.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Organic Synthesis
courses.description: Methods and strategy for the preparation of complex organic compounds.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Organic Synthesis
courses.description: Advanced topics in the synthesis of complex organic molecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to Data Science using Python
courses.description: Basic principles of data science and the application of Python to data science.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Statistical Mechanics
courses.description: Statistical thermodynamics, lattice statistics, molecular distribution and correlation functions, the theories of liquids and solutions, phase transitions, cluster theory, and measurement.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemical Kinetics and Reaction Dynamics
courses.description: Modern theoretical and experimental methods for studying macroscopic and microscopic bimolecular and unimolecular processes are discussed, as are methods for describing complex kinetic systems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemistry of Electronic Organic Materials
courses.description: This course provides a broad description of the basic chemical and physical concepts that determine the properties of electrically active materials.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Computational Chemistry
courses.description: Introductory course in computational chemistry, discussing electronic structure theory, semiemphirical methods, molecular mechanics, transistion-state searching, and computation of thermodynamic quantities.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Quantum Mechanics
courses.description: Important concepts and applications of quantum mechanics at the intermediate level, including operators, perturbation and variational methods applied to atoms and molecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Molecular Spectroscopy
courses.description: Study of energy of electronic transitions in molecules, selection rules, excitation processes, and laser spectroscopy.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry I
courses.description: The chemistry and biochemistry of proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other biomolecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biochemistry II
courses.description: The chemistry and biochemistry of proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, nucleic acids, and other biomolecules.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Chemistry of the Origins of Life
courses.description: Current scientific theories pertaining to the origin of life and early evolution, emphasizing how current knowledge of biology, chemistry and physics limits the possibilities.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Enzymology and Metabolism
courses.description: Structure and chemistry of enzymes, enzyme mechanism, enzyme kinetics, enzyme inhibitors, and medicinal chemistry.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Macromolecular Structure
courses.description: Principles of protein, nucleic acid, and membrane structure. Major emphasis on protein folding, detailed description of three-dimensional structure of proteins and nucleic acids.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Molecular Biochemistry
courses.description: Current topics in molecular biology including eukaryotic transcriptions, RNA processing, repair and recombination, immunity, viruses, DNA fingerprinting, and genome sequencing.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Protein Crystallography
courses.description: Application of crystallographic principles to the structure determination of macromolecules by molecular replacement, multiple isomorphous replacements. High-speed data collection methods and cryocrystallography.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biophysical Chemistry
courses.description: Applications of the principles and techniques of physical chemistry in biochemistry, with emphasis in the equilibrium and dynamic behavior of macromolecules in solution.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Proteomics: Technologies & Applications
courses.description: This workshop-based course explores the field of proteomics with a focus on the technologies used, their advantages/disadvantages, and their applications to real world problems.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Preparation and Reaction of Polymers
courses.description: A detailed treatment of the reactions involved in the synthesis of both human-made and natural polymers, including preparation and degradative reactions of polymer systems. Crosslisted with CHE and PTFE 6750.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Physical Chemistry of Polymer Solutions
courses.description: Study of polymer solutions, polymer miscibility, absorptions, sorptions, plasticization, molecular weights, molecular weight distributions, and interfacial phenomena using thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. Crosslisted with CHE, MSE, and PTFE 6751.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Polymer Characterization
courses.description: This course introduces the student to surface, near-surface, and structural methods of polymer characterization. Specialized techniques critical to physical structure are emphasized. Crosslisted with CHE, MSE, and PTFE 6752.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Theoretical Chemistry of Polymers
courses.description: Thermodynamics and microscopic dynamics of polymers. Fundamental concepts, including scaling concepts, governing anisotropy of polarizability, phase transitions, morphology, time-dependent correlations, etc. are discussed. Crosslisted with MSE and PTFE 6755.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Discovery of Signaling Molecules
courses.description: The diversity of chemical signals between organisms and their structural specificities will be presented along with chemical and biological methods for isolating signaling molecules. Crosslisted with BIOL 6756 and CEE 6756.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Advanced Polymer Chemistry
courses.description: Advanced topics in synthetic polymerization methodology, polymer structure, and polymer properties in solution and the solid state.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Biocatalysis and Metabolic Engineering
courses.description: This course provides in-depth coverage of various topics in biocatalysis and metabolic engineering. Goals of this course are the development of an understanding of proteins as catalysts, their functioning in metabolic networks, their application in various industries, and recognition of their potential for addressing future challenges in science and engineering. Crosslisted with CHBE 6760.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Protein Engineering
courses.description: This course covers the theory and practice of protein engineering methods, including specific examples of engineered proteins and their applications from the literature.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Instrument Design for Astrobiology Missions
courses.description: Students survey the literature, develop an instrument concept, and present it to a review panel in a mock NASA proposal style.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Nanoscale Science and Technology
courses.description: Chemistry and physics of materials, structures, and surfaces with characteristic feature sizes below 100 nm, and their applications in catalysis, electronics, photonics, energy, and biomedicine.

courses.subject: CHEM
courses.title: Introduction to Research
courses.description: Introduction to laboratory techniques, experimental design, library and database searching, presentations.

courses.title: Information Resources for Chemists and Biochemists
